root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before `mrb_str_len_to_dbl()` leaves its pre-copy scan, the next numeric span it will hand to the subsequent float-parsing phase must fit within the fixed local buffer. In the vulnerable original, the scan leaves `pend` at the end of the 73-byte witness and the code later restarts from `s`, so the next span is 73 bytes against a 69-byte payload capacity. The fixed original cuts `pend` at the first trailing space and preserves the trimmed start pointer, reducing the next span to 20 bytes before any copy can happen.
root_cause_criterion.description: The missing source-level guard is that the post-scan numeric span must fit within `buf` before the function proceeds into the vulnerable copy path.
root_cause_criterion.verification_note: The frozen traces differentially confirm this upstream obligation: the vulnerable original records `next_span_bytes=73 > capacity_bytes=69`, while the fixed original records `next_span_bytes=20 <= capacity_bytes=79` on the stock PoC.

nodes.state: At the last observed `*n++ = c` store before AddressSanitizer aborts, the vulnerable original is targeting destination slot 70 while the last in-bounds payload slot of `buf` is 69.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable assertion trace records `copy_store.store_offset=70` and `copy_store.capacity_bytes=69`; the fixed original never reaches `copy_store` on the stock PoC because the upstream span decision exits before the copy loop.

edges.relation: The same end-of-span limit chosen before the copy path (`pend - s == 73` in the vulnerable original) is still the loop bound at the eventual `*n++ = c` store, so the copy loop keeps advancing until it targets a slot past `buf`.
edges.evidence: The vulnerable assertion trace records `span_decision.end_offset == copy_store.end_offset == 73`.
